EEG-first foundation models · Research registry · 18 September 2026

Depth, breadth, and a defensible evaluation boundary.

One catalog for scalp EEG, MEG and invasive recordings. Explore licensing, clinical tasks, language decoding and paired-modality opportunities—without conflating public access, permissive reuse, or independent data.

Metadata inventory, not a training-ready corpus. All raw-signal ingestion remains blocked pending unit, channel, geometry, consent/terms and split audits. Most original metadata was checked on 29 August 2026; new targeted source checks are dated separately. Registry counts are not unique cohorts or subjects.

Filters apply to data-driven charts and tables in all five sections. Research notes remain unfiltered. “Permissive” excludes share-alike, NC, custom, unclear/conflicting terms, restricted access and unverified leads; it is not clearance to release weights.

01 / Pretraining inventory

Scale is more than recording hours.

Breadth means independent people, sites, ages, pathologies, states, devices and montages. Depth means longitudinal coverage, usable duration, signal bandwidth, annotations and synchronized modalities. Keep both; do not let one long cohort dominate the sampling mixture.

Participant breadth × recording depth

Log axes. Only records with positive source-reported participants and hours are plotted. Hover for context; click a dot to visit the dataset. Values are not deduplicated.

Dataset / benchmark intersection

Neural modality coverage

Modalities overlap. “iEEG” may coexist with the more specific SEEG or ECoG label, so these bars must not be summed.

License-aware sampling

Use CC0, CC-BY and ODC-By candidates for the first legal review queue. Keep CC-BY-SA in a separate pool. Public download access does not erase NC terms, DUAs or stimulus copyright.

PhysioNet is not one license: its permissive and restricted collections are separated here. SWEC’s permissive badge conflicts with research-only prose; it is excluded until clarified.

Preserve the signal

Scalp EEG, bipolar clinical EEG, MEG magnetometers/gradiometers, intracranial voltages and spike counts require different units, referencing and bandwidth handling.

The original 256 Hz / common-average / five-second configuration is retained as a reference—not silently applied to the expanded registry.

Known overlap, not extra hours

TUH subsets, HBN release shards, PEERS mirrors, NMT variants, LibriBrain extensions and re-recorded participants carry family or lineage warnings.

03 / Clinical evaluation

Test clinical utility—not just window accuracy.

Published protocols and proposed uses are explicitly separate. A labeled dataset is not automatically a standardized benchmark. A benchmark suite adds no independent recording hours; component licenses still apply.

Clinical domains

Click any domain above to filter the clinical resources below. One resource can serve multiple domains; counts therefore overlap.

Evaluation contract

Seizures: event sensitivity, false alarms per monitoring hour, latency, and held-out sites. Sleep: macro F1, κ, per-stage recall and held-out people/nights. Prognosis: discrimination, calibration, external validation and a fixed causal horizon.

Use frozen probes, controlled fine-tuning, low-label learning curves and external-cohort testing. Reserve test people and benchmark families before self-supervised pretraining—not merely before fitting a classification head.

Browse clinical resources by domain and task

Choose a domain to show only its datasets and benchmark resources. Then optionally narrow to a specific downstream task. These controls affect only the clinical table; the catalog filters above still apply.

Domain
Other benchmark references and proposed non-clinical tasks

Assistive communication, general representation testing and cognitive tasks may complement the clinical battery. Protocol status remains explicit.

Alpha–delta ratio and delayed cerebral ischemia

ADR is a long-studied quantitative EEG feature, not a new 2026 invention. Predicting ADR from the same EEG window is mainly a signal-processing surrogate; forecasting an independently adjudicated future DCI event is a different clinical target. Start with a transparent spectral baseline and report the band definitions, reference, normalization and artifacts.

BDSP SAH/DCI is directly relevant but requires a restricted-use agreement. A 2026 ADR study links a Figshare deposit whose raw EEG content and data license were not verified here. Neither is admitted to the permissive training pool.

Source context: Claassen et al., 2004 · automated EEG/DCI prediction study. Sedation, sleep, seizures, artifacts and reference changes are important competing explanations; do not infer a deployable threshold from a small retrospective study.

03 / Language-specific inventory

Reading, listening and producing language are different tests.

Free-text decoding, closed-set classification, stimulus retrieval and clinical report alignment should never share an undifferentiated “brain-to-text” score. Motor and ocular correlates can dominate a weak experimental protocol.

Non-invasive EEG

ZuCo and PEERS provide language-related cognitive tasks; inner-speech collections often use small fixed vocabularies. P300 spelling is stimulus-driven assistive communication, not unrestricted thought decoding.

Mandatory controls: EOG/eye-tracking or EMG-only baselines, prompt timing, held-out sentence content, and language-model-only or brain-ablated comparisons.

MEG and typed text

MEG-MASC supports speech perception. LibriBrain/LibriBrain100 are large listening resources but non-commercial. Brain2Qwerty v1 is public under NC terms; its EEG and MEG are not simultaneous pairs. V2 data remains embargoed on the project page.

Typing-related signals do not demonstrate decoding arbitrary unexpressed thoughts. Some LibriBrain2 competition data remains withheld.

Invasive language signals

Brain Treebank captures speech perception in ECoG/SEEG; Willett’s intracortical speech and handwriting data target attempted output. Tiny participant counts make subject transfer an open experimental question.

Clinical EEG reports are another useful alignment target, but represent a clinician’s interpretation—not the participant’s intended utterance.

Scoring recommendation: use CER/WER for actual sequence generation; chance-corrected classification for fixed vocabularies; recall@K with a stated candidate pool for retrieval. Report all preprocessing, language-model priors, within-person calibration and neural ablations. Repeated stories/sentences must be grouped across splits.
04 / Research direction · Proposed, not established

Learn what the invasive teacher can teach the scalp student.

A strong non-invasive encoder may improve estimation of shared neural processes. That is a more defensible aim than claiming it can reconstruct every local intracranial signal that never reaches the scalp.

Your ultrasound–MRI analogy

The fetal ultrasound–MRI study combines JEPA-inspired masked ultrasound latent prediction with separate cross-modal contrastive alignment and MRI-informed targets. It does not establish exact reconstruction of the expensive modality from the cheap one.

The useful analogy is privileged training information: a teacher available during training shapes an encoder used alone at inference. Joint training on two unpaired corpora, by itself, does not identify which moments or latent sources correspond.

The measurement limit

x_scalp = L_scalp · s + ε_scalp
x_invasive = L_invasive · s + ε_invasive

Different source configurations can produce similar scalp measurements. Better representation learning can improve estimation under learned priors; it cannot guarantee recovery of arbitrary information absent from those measurements. Predict shared, stable targets and retain uncertainty.

Paired and partially paired resources

“Simultaneous” is not enough: align clocks, triggers, reference and bandwidth. Same-subject separate sessions or common-stimulus data provide weaker correspondence and are labeled accordingly.

01 · SCALEScalp-first JEPA

Pretrain on a license-screened, deduplicated EEG mixture. Balance datasets, patients, pathologies and recording states; retain multiscale temporal features.

02 · TEACHERSeparate invasive encoder

Learn local physiological features with modality-specific sampling and coordinates. Define low-frequency, regional or event targets that have a plausible scalp correlate.

03 · BRIDGECalibrate on synchronized pairs

Use a small paired cohort to train an EEG predictor against stopped-gradient teacher targets. Keep shared and modality-private latents; add a variance-preserving objective.

04 · FALSIFYValidate without the teacher

Hold out people, sites and content. Compare against scalp-only JEPA, shuffled/time-shifted pairs, simple spectral features and equal-compute controls.

A concrete objective to prototype
L = L_EEG-JEPA + λ_pair · L_shared(z_EEG, stopgrad(z_invasive))
+ λ_task · L_task + λ_var · L_variance

This is a proposed design, not a result from the catalog. Use local time/region correspondence where available. A small predictor should map EEG latents into only the teacher’s predictable shared subspace. Cross-modal retrieval can be an auxiliary diagnostic; distribution matching alone can align the wrong semantics. Stop-gradient alone does not prevent collapse.

For unpaired corpora, pretrain separate teachers, condition on known anatomy or common stimuli, and use a small paired set to resolve correspondence. A MEG teacher may be useful where measured simultaneous EEG–MEG is available. Synthetic forward models supply controlled priors—not substitutes for real paired validation.

Decisive experiments and failure modes
  1. Use ds004752 and Boran’s collection as pairing candidates, but resolve possible participant overlap before counting or splitting them.
  2. Compare identical scalp architectures and compute budgets: EEG-only JEPA; paired teacher alignment; unpaired/domain matching; shuffled and time-shifted pairs.
  3. Measure downstream clinical performance and held-out cross-modal prediction separately. Good classification does not establish faithful invasive-signal recovery.
  4. Use no-brain/noise, EOG/EMG-only and language-model-only controls for language tasks. Hold out stimulus content and remove future information for forecasting.
  5. Estimate patient/site-level uncertainty; do not treat millions of adjacent windows from nine patients as millions of independent biological examples.
Practical guardrails for this repository

Each TOML carries roles, modalities, task domains, measurement provenance, source URLs, data-license screening, access status, pairing level, benchmark protocol status, overlap families and ingestion blockers. Original coordinate audits and snapshot fields are preserved. Rebuilds consume TOMLs; they do not replace curated fields with a discovery crawl.

No total-hour claim is made across overlapping studies. Partial benchmark component graphs are explicitly partial. The raw download/reader layer, exhaustive source rechecks, exact patient-level exclusion manifests and official benchmark scorers remain separate implementation work.

Self-contained, offline HTML · No tracking or external JavaScript · Registry generated from versioned TOMLs · Figures summarize metadata, not independently validated clinical evidence.
Primary references and field caveats are available through each row’s Details panel. Clickable markers open publisher pages. Original 375-schema audit is preserved in the repository.
